desc: The MJ-12 corpus originates in a roll of undeveloped 35mm film that arrived anonymously, postmarked Albuquerque, at the Los Angeles home of television producer Jaime Shandera on 11 December 1984. Developed, it produced an eight-page 'Briefing Document: Operation Majestic 12' dated 18 November 1952, prepared for President-elect Eisenhower, naming twelve officials and describing the recovery of a crashed disc and four bodies near Roswell. Shandera, Bill Moore and Stanton Friedman released it publicly in May 1987. The National Archives searched Air Force, Joint Chiefs, NSC, Truman Library and Eisenhower Library holdings and found nothing except a single document in Record Group 341: the Cutler-Twining memorandum of 14 July 1954, whose problems NARA itself enumerated - no Top Secret register number, no letterhead or watermark, a security marking that NSC's FOIA office says post-dates the Eisenhower administration, and a paper stock ('diction onionskin') inconsistent with the Eisenhower Library's sample. The FBI investigated and states an Air Force investigation determined the document to be a fake. The board's position is that the MJ-12 documents are best understood not as evidence of a 1947 committee but as evidence of a 1980s operation: the Albuquerque postmark, the Doty and Moore connections, and the discovery of a planted-looking document inside a federal record group all point at the same place at the same time as the Bennewitz campaign.

dossier.denialPosture: This is one of the few nodes on the board carrying a denial that is a directed act by a named denier. AARO's Historical Record Report is recorded as the denier, and the form the denial takes is omission: the report tasked with resolving the historical record does not address the corpus at all. Alongside that sits the FBI's account of an Air Force investigation that determined the document to be a fake, and NARA's itemised findings against the Cutler-Twining memorandum. The board's reading is that the paper is a forgery and the omission is still worth recording, because those are separate facts about separate institutions.
dossier.narrative:
Every institutional body that has examined this corpus has rejected it, and the rejections are unusually specific. The National Archives searched Air Force, Joint Chiefs, National Security Council, Truman Library and Eisenhower Library holdings and came back with one item: the Cutler-Twining memorandum. NARA then enumerated what was wrong with it. There is no Top Secret register number. It sits in a folder containing no other MJ-12 material. It has no official letterhead and no watermark. Its 'Top Secret Restricted Information' marking is one the NSC's own FOIA office says did not come into use until the Nixon administration, which is to say two presidencies after the date on the paper. NARA's conservation specialist determined the sheet was a ribbon copy prepared on diction onionskin. The FBI's own account is blunter still: an Air Force investigation determined the document to be a fake.

The board's position is therefore not that the documents are disputed but that they are the wrong kind of object to dispute. They are dated 1952 and they behave like an artefact of 1984. The film arrived postmarked Albuquerque in December 1984; the AQUARIUS paper had been shown at Kirtland in April 1983; Moore has admitted cooperating with AFOSI; Richard Doty served as the conduit in the parallel Bennewitz and Howe channels. That is one city, one twenty-month window and one set of people. The board grades the inference Tier 3 and states its reasoning rather than its conclusion, because a concentration in place and time is a pattern and not a proof.

The most consequential fact about the corpus on this board is a silence. AARO's Historical Record Report of March 2024, tasked with resolving exactly this kind of allegation, does not address MJ-12 or AQUARIUS at all. Two of the most persistent alleged programme names in the entire historical record are absent from the report written to settle the historical record. Whatever the documents are, their omission is a fact about the report rather than about them.
openQuestions: Nobody has ever identified who sent the film. The postmark is the only physical lead in the record and it establishes a city, not a sender.

The eight-page briefing document itself has not been opened as a primary artefact for this board. What the board holds is the FBI's file, NARA's findings on the Cutler-Twining memorandum and the secondary literature; the corpus is characterised through its examiners rather than read directly.

How a document with the physical characteristics NARA described came to be inside Record Group 341 is unexplained by any record opened here. NARA established what the paper is; no opened record establishes how it got into the file.
dossier.whatItIs: A corpus of purported briefing papers that entered the public record as a roll of undeveloped 35mm film, postmarked Albuquerque, delivered anonymously to the Los Angeles home of television producer Jaime Shandera on 11 December 1984. Developed, the film produced an eight-page 'Briefing Document: Operation Majestic 12' dated 18 November 1952 and addressed to President-elect Eisenhower, naming twelve officials and describing the recovery of a crashed disc and four bodies near Roswell. Shandera, William L. Moore and Stanton Friedman released it publicly in May 1987. The only associated paper ever located inside a federal record group is the Cutler-Twining memorandum of 14 July 1954, found in Record Group 341.
dossier.whyImplicated: The corpus is on this board as a forgery with a provenance, not as evidence of a 1947 committee. It matters because the same city, the same interval and the same handful of intermediaries produced the Bennewitz material and the AQUARIUS paper, and because a document with the physical characteristics of a plant was found sitting inside a National Archives record group. A fabricated briefing paper is a curiosity. A fabricated briefing paper that arrives through an Air Force Office of Special Investigations channel and turns up filed in a federal record series is an operation, and the question the board keeps open is who ran it.
